verdict.line: You win the lane from level 2 through roughly level 11 if you punish every missed Q (Infected Cleaver); you lose relevance once Mundo finishes two full items and his R (Maximum Dosage) sustain outpaces your damage.

brief.thesis: Sett's R (The Show Stopper) deals damage based on the target's current max HP, and Mundo is the single best max-HP stacker in the game, so every landed ult from full build hits him for a brutal chunk regardless of armor. The lane hinges on Mundo having zero hard CC to stop your W (Haymaker) taunt into E (Facebreaker) stun, meaning every all-in window opens the moment his Q is down.

theirWindow.when: Right after his Q lands on you
theirWindow.what: He gets a burst of AD from Blunt Force Trauma's passive scaling plus his Q heal, and will chain into an E-empowered auto to snowball the trade. Back off, let your passive Grit shield build, and don't trade autos into his empowered E swing.

yourWindow.when: His Q is thrown and missed
yourWindow.what: Instantly walk up and all-in: charge W for the taunt (hold at least 1 second), then E for the stun on the taunted target, weaving in your Q3 empowered auto. He has no CC to punish this and Infected Cleaver's cooldown at early ranks is long enough to fully commit.

start.why: The passive HP regen and damage reduction on the next hit directly offsets Mundo's Q poke and lets you win extended trades instead of losing the war of attrition.

boots.why: Mundo's Q, empowered W auto, and E all deal physical damage; the flat reduction shrinks every poke and trade he throws at you.

core.why: The attack speed and burst-damage proc lets you win the auto-attack war during your all-in windows and scales your Q3 empowered hit.
The on-hit true damage proc and healing spike give you a second burst threshold to force fights before he tops off HP.
The tenacity and shield turn your all-ins into fights he can't just tank through with raw HP, and blunts any late CC his team brings.

situational.when: he is snowballing off Q heals and E sustain and you need grievous wounds to shut it down
he outscales you and you need to survive his empowered-E burst windows in teamfights
he starts building pure HP/armor and you need armor penetration plus grievous wounds together

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained stacking through repeated short trades matches how you fight Mundo, and the healing from full stacks offsets his Q sustain instead of losing the war of attrition.

summoners.why: Ignite is the single best tool against Mundo's early sustain — it neutralizes the Q heal and Blunt Force Trauma's healback during your level 2-5 all-in windows and can outright secure kills he'd otherwise survive.

playing.title: Sidestep every Q
playing.detail: Infected Cleaver has a slow travel time and long early cooldown; dodging it removes his only real poke and heal source, and punishing the miss is your biggest all-in trigger.

playing.title: Lead with charged W
playing.detail: Hold Haymaker for at least a full second to guarantee the taunt before following with E's stun — Mundo has no ability to interrupt this sequence.

playing.title: Track your Grit bar
playing.detail: Pit Grit's shield caps damage taken during trades; time your all-ins for when the shield is up so his E burst doesn't outright win the exchange.

playing.title: Don't auto-trade past two items
playing.detail: Once Mundo has Heart Zapper stacks and HP items online, his empowered third auto and E burst start winning straight trades — shift to poke-and-disengage instead.

playing.title: Save all-ins around his R usage
playing.detail: Maximum Dosage gives him a large heal-over-time and move speed burst; don't commit resources into a fresh R, but punish him hard in the window right before he's forced to use it.

playing.title: Prioritize R on him in skirmishes
playing.detail: The Show Stopper scales off max HP, so landing it on Mundo specifically over squishier targets often deals more raw damage — grab him first in any teamfight he's in.

playing.title: Push and reset before 20 minutes
playing.detail: Your lane dominance window closes once he completes his first two items; use the earlier levels to shove waves, take plates, and pressure objectives rather than staying to out-scale him.

brief.patchCaveat: Item and rune names reflect the mythic-removed item system and Season 2024-2025 rune tree as I last saw it; verify Trinity Force, Sundered Sky, Steraks Gage, and Chempunk Chainsword are still live and check current numbers on Infected Cleaver's cooldown and The Show Stopper's max-HP scaling before locking in, since balance patches shift these frequently.
